```sql
WITH l AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           ol.order_id,
           pv.id AS variant_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
s AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           sum(quantity)         AS quantity,
           sum(line_total_cents) AS revenue_cents
      FROM l
     GROUP BY product_id
),
oc AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS order_count
      FROM (SELECT product_id, order_id FROM l GROUP BY product_id, order_id) x
     GROUP BY product_id
),
vc AS (
    SELECT product_id, count(*) AS variant_count
      FROM (SELECT product_id, variant_id FROM l GROUP BY product_id, variant_id) y
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       oc.order_count,
       s.quantity,
       s.revenue_cents,
       vc.variant_count
  FROM s
  JOIN products p ON p.id = s.product_id
  JOIN oc         ON oc.product_id = s.product_id
  JOIN vc         ON vc.product_id = s.product_id
 ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De dure externe sort op (p.id, o.id) voor de `count(DISTINCT ...)` wordt vervangen door hash-aggregaties op een eenmalig gematerialiseerde join-set. Daarbij worden de distinct-paren apart geteld, wat dezelfde aantallen oplevert. De sommen worden in één stap over dezelfde rijen berekend, zodat waarden en types gelijk blijven. `products` wordt pas na de aggregatie gejoind, en omdat `p.id` uniek is blijven de groepen identiek aan het origineel.
